answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewal cannot meet the 18% mandate this cycle, and negotiate_terms is effectively foreclosed for now. The low-cost vendor's quote meets the mandate outright, and memory_c2 records a prior clean switch (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing), making switch_primary_vendor the leading candidate. However, the line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so any onboarding friction with a new primary supplier carries outsized delivery risk that memory_c2's single archived case may not fully represent — worth confirming the original record wasn't cherry-picked or missing caveats. I also want to check memory_c3 (second-sourcing mitigated a single point of failure) to see whether a hedged approach — qualifying the low-cost vendor as primary while retaining the incumbent in a limited secondary capacity — is feasible, since that would capture the cost savings while preserving a safety net against the no-buffer condition. Given the stakes (contract expiring in 14 days, no slack in production), I favor a small guarded test of the vendor switch on a limited SKU/volume slice rather than a full cutover, to validate onboarding claims before committing the whole primary volume.
